subtitle: كتاب الأنوار والمراقب — The Book of Lights and Watchtowers
author: Yaʿqūb al-Qirqisānī (10th c.)
intro: The opening of the great 10th-century Karaite summa, in its original Arabic (ed. Nemoy, Yale 1939–43, vol. I; orthography lightly normalized). Qirqisānī lays down the manifesto that governs the whole book: religious obligations must be reached by baḥth (inquiry) and naẓar (rational speculation), and the truth is to be accepted from whoever holds it — Rabbanite, ʿAnanite, or anyone else — even a view no one ever held before. He defends reason against the Karaites who fear it, praises Daniel al-Qūmisī, and explains why sectarian rancour drove him to compose the work — closing on Psalm 119. Note: this text is in Arabic script (not Hebrew-letter Judeo-Arabic); hover a phrase to light up its English, tap any word for the panel, and tap the dotted key terms for notes.

source.edition: Leon Nemoy, Kitāb al-Anwār wa'l-Marāqib (Yale, 1939–43), vol. I, Maqāla I, Bāb 1 (ṣadr al-kitāb); collated with the Cairo 2019 edition.
source.note: The ṣadr is fragmentary at its head and opens mid-sentence ('…I know neither ʿAnan nor Benjamin…'). Embedded Hebrew citations are kept in Hebrew script as in the source.

terms.note: With al-naẓar, one of the two key methodological terms of the whole Anwār. Qirqisānī pairs baḥth (the active search) and naẓar (rational reflection) as the joint instrument by which religious obligations must be established — the move that aligns him with the Muʿtazilite kalām of his day.

Rational inspection of a question. For Qirqisānī, whatever naẓar makes necessary must be adopted 'from whoever holds it' — Rabbanite, ʿAnanite, or other. The classic Tibbonid Hebrew rendering is ha-ʿiyyun.

terms.gloss: the intelligible; what is grasped by reason
terms.note: The domain of rational knowledge — logic, dialectic, philosophy. The Karaite quietists Qirqisānī attacks fault anyone who 'speculates on the maʿqūl'; he answers that it is the very foundation on which every claim is built.
Literally the 'external' sciences: fields outside Scripture — dialectic (al-jadaliyya) and philosophy (al-falsafiyya), and by extension logic. Compare al-Fārābī's contemporary survey Iḥṣāʾ al-ʿulūm.

With al-kathra ('the majority'), a loaded term in Karaite–Rabbanite polemic: the Rabbanites rest the truth of religion on the chain of transmission and the weight of the majority — a claim Qirqisānī sets out to answer.
Paired here with al-jumhūr. The appeal to numbers — that most of the nation followed the Rabbanite masters — is exactly the argument Qirqisānī subordinates to baḥth and naẓar.
An honorific for Bet Hillel and Bet Shammai: those who command the Hebrew tongue and stand at the root of transmission. Qirqisānī concedes their standing while insisting reason still arbitrates.

aligned.ja: المقالة الأولى · الباب الأول: صدر الكتاب
aligned.en: Discourse I · Chapter 1: The Book's Opening

aligned.ja: [...لا أعرف لا «عانان» ولا] بنيامين ولا غيرهما من هذه الطبقة، إذ هم خوارج كانوا بالأمم؛ وإنما أعرف בית הלל وבית שמאי، الذين هم الأصل، وهم الذين كانوا بقرب النبوة،
aligned.en: [...I know neither ʿAnan nor] Benjamin nor any other of this sect — for they are dissenters who arose among the nations. I know only Bet Hillel and Bet Shammai, who are the root, and who were close to prophecy,

pairs.en: they are dissenters who arose among the nations

aligned.ja: وهم أخذوا عن الأنبياء وعنهم نقلوا، وهم أهل اللغة، وهم الكثرة والجمهور.
aligned.en: and who took from the prophets and transmitted from them; they are the masters of the language, and they are the majority and the multitude.

aligned.ja: فإن قال قائل: هذا أحق بالقول ممن يضيف إلى الربانيين «عانان» ويجعل سبيله في الأصلية سبيلهم — فإن هذا لا يجوز؛ وإنما يجب أن تُتخذ الفرائض بالبحث والنظر.
aligned.en: Should someone object that this deserves to be said more than of one who attaches ʿAnan to the Rabbanites and treats the fundamentals as they do — that is not permissible. Rather, the obligations must be arrived at through inquiry and speculation.

pairs.en: the obligations must be arrived at

aligned.ja: فكلَّما أوجبه النظر وساق إليه البحث، كان هو الذي يجب اتخاذه، من قول مَن كان: إما الربانيين، وإما «عانان»، وإما غيرهما.
aligned.en: Whatever speculation makes necessary and inquiry leads to — that is what must be adopted, from the words of whoever it may be: whether the Rabbanites, or ʿAnan, or anyone else.

pairs.en: that is what must be adopted
from the words of whoever it may be

aligned.ja: نعم، ولو ظهر للبحّاث النظّار قولٌ لم يقل به أحد بتة، لوجب قبوله، بشرط ألا يكون عليه طعن ولا يلحقه فساد.
aligned.en: Indeed — even if there appeared to the inquiring speculators a view that no one had ever held, accepting it would be obligatory, provided no objection stands against it and no flaw attaches to it.

pairs.en: even if there appeared to the inquiring speculators

pairs.ja: قولٌ لم يقل به أحد بتة
pairs.en: a view that no one had ever held

aligned.ja: فأما الطبقة الأخرى، المنسوبون إلى أنهم من القرائين، فمنهم الفرس، مثل قوم من التُّسْتَريين ومن مال إليهم.
aligned.en: As for the other group, those who count themselves among the Karaites — among them are the Persians, such as a circle of the Tustarīs and those who incline to them.

aligned.ja: فإنهم — مع إظهارهم وادعائهم للبحث — يعيبون على من نظر في المعقول، يعني بشيء من العلوم البرانية، إما الجدلية وإما الفلسفية.
aligned.en: For they — despite their show of, and claim to, inquiry — fault anyone who speculates on the intelligible, that is, on any of the 'outer' sciences, whether dialectic or philosophy.

pairs.en: despite their show of, and claim to, inquiry

pairs.ja: يعيبون على من نظر في المعقول
pairs.en: fault anyone who speculates on the intelligible

aligned.ja: والذي قطعهم عن ذلك أمران: أحدهما الكسل عن طلب معرفة ذلك وصعوبته عليهم وطلب الراحة من التعب؛
aligned.en: Two things cut them off from this: the first is laziness about seeking such knowledge, its difficulty for them, and the wish to rest from toil;

pairs.en: Two things cut them off from this
and the wish to rest from toil

aligned.ja: والثاني أن بعضهم يتوهم أن النظر في المعقول يُفسد مَن يشتغل به ويُخرجه عن الدين، لأنهم زعموا أنهم رأوا قوما ممن طلب ذلك قد فسدت أديانهم.
aligned.en: the second is that some of them imagine that speculating on the intelligible corrupts whoever engages in it and drives him out of religion — for they claimed to have seen people who pursued it whose faith had been ruined.

pairs.en: the second is that some of them imagine

pairs.ja: النظر في المعقول يُفسد مَن يشتغل به
pairs.en: speculating on the intelligible corrupts whoever engages in it
and drives him out of religion

aligned.ja: وهذا سبب الريبة والتهمة، إذ كان قولهم هذا يوهم السامع أن المعقول يضاد الدين وينافره ويباينه؛ فإن كان ذلك كذلك، فإن الدين مطعون عليه، وهذا غاية المحال.
aligned.en: This is the source of the suspicion and the charge: their saying this makes the hearer suppose that the intelligible opposes religion, conflicts with it, and is at odds with it. Yet if that were so, then religion itself would stand discredited — and that is the height of absurdity.

pairs.en: This is the source of the suspicion and the charge
then religion itself would stand discredited
and that is the height of absurdity

aligned.ja: وسنبيِّن أن المعقول أصلٌ يُبنى عليه كل قول، ويُستخرج به كل علم.
aligned.en: And we shall show that the intelligible is a foundation on which every claim is built and by which every science is derived.

pairs.en: that the intelligible is a foundation
on which every claim is built
and by which every science is derived

aligned.ja: ولم أرَ أحدا من منتحلي النظر أنصحَ لنفسه من دانيال القومسي، ولا مَن يُعطي النظرَ حقه ويوفيه ما يجب له مثلَه.
aligned.en: I have not seen anyone among those who profess speculation more sincere with himself than Daniel al-Qūmisī, nor anyone who gives speculation its due and renders what it deserves as he does.

pairs.ja: ولم أرَ أحدا من منتحلي النظر
pairs.en: I have not seen anyone among those who profess speculation

aligned.ja: وذلك أن كل ما أظهره له النظر، وساقه إليه البحث، وأوجبته عليه الحجة — انتقل إليه واتخذه.
aligned.en: For everything that speculation disclosed to him, that inquiry led him to, and that proof made binding upon him — he moved over to it and adopted it.

pairs.en: everything that speculation disclosed to him
and that proof made binding upon him
he moved over to it and adopted it

aligned.ja: إلا أنه قد لحقه عيبٌ أزرى به عند قوم من أصحابنا، وهو إفراطه في بغض العنانية ونصبُه نفسه لهم بالعداوة.
aligned.en: Yet a fault clung to him that lowered him in the eyes of some of our colleagues: his excess in hating the ʿAnanites and his setting himself against them in enmity.

pairs.ja: أزرى به عند قوم من أصحابنا
pairs.en: that lowered him in the eyes of some of our colleagues
his excess in hating the ʿAnanites
his setting himself against them in enmity

aligned.ja: وقد كان في أول أمره يفضّل «عانان» ويذكره في كتبه كثيرا ويزعم أنه ראש המשכילים، ثم صار من بعد ذلك يقول إنه ראש הטיפשים؛ وهذا من مثله قبيح جدا، مع ما هو عليه من المعرفة والنُّسك.
aligned.en: At first he used to exalt ʿAnan, mention him often in his books, and claim he was 'the chief of the enlightened'; later he came to call him 'the chief of the fools.' From one like him this is deeply unbecoming — for all his learning and ascetic piety.

pairs.en: At first he used to exalt ʿAnan
mention him often in his books
From one like him this is deeply unbecoming
for all his learning and ascetic piety

aligned.ja: وهذا أيضا أحد البلايا العظيمة التي تعرِض لقوم من أصحابنا: مناصبة بعضهم بعضا، والقصد بالبغضة والعداوة، وأكثر ما يحملهم على ذلك الحسد وطلب الرئاسة.
aligned.en: This too is one of the great afflictions that befall some of our colleagues: their setting upon one another and their bent toward hatred and enmity — and what most drives them to it is envy and the craving for leadership.

pairs.en: that befall some of our colleagues
their bent toward hatred and enmity
envy and the craving for leadership

aligned.ja: فهذا الذي ذكرته هو الذي حرّكني على جمع هذا الكتاب وتأليفه: أريد أن أحكي فيه جُملا من أقاويل العلماء واحتجاجاتهم.
aligned.en: It is just this that moved me to assemble and compose this book: I mean to set down in it a digest of the scholars' statements and their arguments.

pairs.en: to assemble and compose this book
a digest of the scholars' statements

aligned.ja: وأجتهد أن يكون متوسطا بين الإطناب والاختصار: لا يَجِلّ عن عالم، ولا يَدِقّ عن متعلم.
aligned.en: And I shall strive that it be midway between long-windedness and over-brevity: not too weighty for the learned, nor too subtle for the student.

pairs.en: not too weighty for the learned
nor too subtle for the student

aligned.ja: وبالخالق — تعالى جدُّه — وعلى كل خير أستعين، وإليه أرغب فيما رغب إليه فيه عبده ووليه דוד عليه السلام، إذ يقول: גַּל עֵינַי וְאַבִּיטָה נִפְלָאוֹת מִתּוֹרָתֶךָ. גֵּר אָנֹכִי בָאָרֶץ אַל תַּסְתֵּר מִמֶּנִּי מִצְוֹתֶיךָ.
aligned.en: Upon the Creator — exalted be His majesty — and upon all good I rely; and I beseech Him for what His servant and friend David, peace be upon him, besought when he said: 'Open my eyes, that I may behold wonders out of Your Torah. I am a stranger in the land; hide not Your commandments from me.' (Ps. 119:18–19)

pairs.en: and upon all good I rely
